title: Nuevo Laredo Launches Paisano Winter Operation to Welcome Thousands Home for the Holidays — and a Toy Drive for Kids
excerpt: Nuevo Laredo has launched its winter operation to welcome home thousands of Mexican nationals returning through the border for the holidays, plus a toy...
content:
Nuevo Laredo has launched its winter operation to welcome home thousands of Mexican nationals returning through the border for the holidays — and, alongside it, a toy drive asking families and businesses to make sure local children have something under the tree.

The “Heroínas y Héroes Paisanos” Winter Operation 2026 runs from November 25, 2026 through January 8, 2027. The Nuevo Laredo government, led by Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas, is carrying it out with Tamaulipas Governor Américo Villarreal Anaya and federal authorities, offering roadside assistance, guidance and tourism information to paisanos traveling through the city on their way home for the season.

The operation is the holiday-season counterpart to the caravans that already pass through the border each December. For many families on both sides of the river, it is the first official welcome they meet after a long drive from the interior of the United States.

The city is also running its Juguetón 2026 toy drive, inviting families and businesses to donate new or gently used non-violent toys through December 4. And on November 25, the municipal women's institute marked the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women by distributing orange ribbons and holding talks on recognizing physical, psychological, economic and sexual violence.

As temperatures drop, Nuevo Laredo's Civil Protection and Fire Department is also running its Operativo Carrusel patrols, handing out hot drinks and blankets to people on the street, families waiting outside hospitals, and anyone exposed to the cold in the early morning and at night. In an emergency, the department reminds residents to call 911.

Sources: Nuevo Laredo Comunica / TNT News Nuevo Laredo, Nov. 26, 2026; Gobierno Municipal de Nuevo Laredo.
